Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus`
Clause-②: **borderline — declare what you find.** No declaration moves and no surface widens; but a predicate that today faults **open** begins evaluating, so the *accept/reject behaviour a host observes* changes. Treat it as declared and say so in the report.
Serial constraints cleared: `packages/components/**` — no in-flight claim. Concurrent siblings: #5927 (`packages/types/src/zod/**`), #5565 (`apps/console` + a seam in `packages/app-shell`), #5835 (`packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx`), #5856 (`examples/schema-catalog/**` + `content/docs/plugins/**`). Disjoint by full path.

## 裁决 — the grade is in the card body, and it is a Bug

Triage seat, 2026-08-24, rebuilt from objectstack#11411 through the documented file-at-destination channel (the source card is closed as moved). Graded **Bug** on this basis, verbatim: *"ADR-0068 D1's stated goal — 'a predicate authored against any one form evaluates identically' — is the declared contract this asymmetry violates … declared≠enforced restoration, not new surface."*

**The measured asymmetry** (⚠️ re-verify every line reference before editing — the card says so itself):

| Site | `current_user` bound? | Evidence |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Page component, app/nav `visible` | **yes** | `packages/app-shell/src/providers/ExpressionProvider.tsx:59,70` |
| Per-option `visibleWhen` | **yes** | `packages/core/src/evaluator/optionRules.ts:103` forwards `scope`; `resolveCascadingOptions(…, predicateScope)` at `form.tsx:1428,2129` |
| Form **section / field** `visibleWhen` | **no** | all three `resolveFieldRuleState` call sites — `form.tsx:1201`, `:1237`, `:1935` — pass `undefined` for `scope`; `predicateScope` is read at `:1276` and used **only** for `resolveCascadingOptions` |

`evalFieldPredicate` (`packages/core/src/evaluator/fieldRules.ts:158`) binds `{ record, previous, extra: scope }`, so with `scope === undefined` a form field's predicate sees `record` and `previous` and nothing else.

**The indicated fix is small and local:** pass `predicateScope` — already in hand at `form.tsx:1276` — as the `scope` argument to the three `resolveFieldRuleState` calls, exactly as `resolveCascadingOptions` already receives it.

## ⛔ Premise-first STOP condition — carried verbatim from the card

> **if you find a recorded ruling that form-field predicates deliberately exclude `current_user`** (the record-purity / per-keystroke-cost design story the source card sketches), **stop and report a fork — ⛔ do not pick a side silently.**

⚠️ Take this seriously and search for it before writing code: ADR-0068, the `fieldRules` / `optionRules` history, and the objectstack cards this one descends from (#11034, #11411, and #11258 → this repo's #5926). "Record purity" is a coherent design position — a field predicate that reads only the record re-evaluates cheaply per keystroke and is referentially transparent. If someone ruled that deliberately, this card is a **fork for the maintainer**, not a fix. ⛔ Do not resolve it yourself in either direction.

## ⚠️ This fix CHANGES USER-VISIBLE BEHAVIOUR, and it must be loud

Carried verbatim: *"predicates that today fault-open on form fields will begin evaluating, and any resolving FALSE will start hiding fields that are currently visible. That is the correctness restoration, but it must be loud."*

Note the direction: `resolveFieldRuleState` passes `true` as the visibility fallback, so **a gate that faults today shows the field to everyone**. That is the dangerous direction, and it is why this is graded a Bug rather than an enhancement — but it also means a host who authored a `visibleWhen` naming `current_user`, saw the field render, and concluded the rule was permissive will now see it hide. Required:

- **The changeset names the change** in those terms — not "binds `current_user`", but "predicates that silently failed open now evaluate, and a rule resolving false now hides the field".
- **A pin per binding surface**, so the three-site parity cannot silently regress. ✅ That is the deliverable that outlives the one-line fix: the defect exists because two of three surfaces got `scope` and one did not, and only a parity pin makes the next divergence loud.

## ⛔ Not a rider — the cross-repo docs follow-up is the PM's, not yours

Carried verbatim: *"objectstack's `content/docs/protocol/objectui/layout-dsl.mdx` binding table was just split (#11034) to document today's asymmetry. When this lands, that row is wrong again in the other direction — the accepting seat files the follow-up docs card in objectstack at landing time (with `Blocked-by:` this card), ⛔ not as a rider on this PR."*

✅ **This seat has taken that obligation** and will file the objectstack card when your PR lands. ⛔ Do not touch objectstack, and ⛔ do not edit that binding table from here.

## PM mechanism assumptions — measure, do not assume

1. **Every line reference in the card is from an objectstack checkout of unknown vintage** (`origin/main` @ `365e334` on the *other* repo, with objectui "at its then-current checkout"). The card itself says re-verify each one. ⛔ Do not work from the table — re-derive all six references (`form.tsx:1201/:1237/:1276/:1428/:1935/:2129`, `fieldRules.ts:158`, `optionRules.ts:103`, `ExpressionProvider.tsx:59,70`) on **your** merge-base and report the delta.
2. ⚠️ **"Pass `predicateScope` to the three calls" is the card's hypothesis, not a measurement.** Verify that `predicateScope` at `:1276` is actually in scope at all three call sites and carries the same shape `resolveCascadingOptions` consumes. If one of the three sits outside that binding, ⛔ **stop and report** — a fix that lands on two of three sites re-creates this exact defect at a smaller scale.
3. **`resolveFieldRuleState`'s `true` visibility fallback is load-bearing to the severity claim.** Confirm it in that function's own source. If it actually fails *closed*, the card's whole "silent and fail-open in the dangerous direction" framing inverts and you should say so before fixing anything.
4. ⚠️ **#5926 is the sibling card and is NOT this one** (`emptyAction` bypass, a second evaluator with an opposite `data` binding, total silence on fault). ⛔ Do not fold it in. If your work touches a site #5926 names, report the overlap rather than absorbing it.

## Verification

**The pin is the deliverable; the one-line fix is not.** Pin all three binding surfaces — page/app-nav, per-option, and form section/field — against the *same* authored predicate, asserting they evaluate identically. That is ADR-0068 D1's stated contract, and a pin on one surface cannot express it.

Direction predicted **before** running: revert the `scope` argument on one of the three call sites and show the parity pin goes **red naming that surface**. **Counter-probe required, and it is the important half:** a predicate that resolves **true** must still render the field on all three surfaces — otherwise "the predicate is now evaluated" is satisfiable by hiding everything, which is a worse bug than fail-open and is invisible to the positive assertion alone. Add the fault case too: a predicate naming a genuinely unbound root must still be shown to fail-open (that is existing behaviour this card does not change) — so the pin distinguishes *"evaluated and false"* from *"faulted"*.

Prove every mutation on disk by grepping the injected text **and separately** the removed text (an editor's exit code proves nothing on a zero-hit anchor). ⚠️ **Print the landing site of each mutation rather than assuming it** — a mis-anchored mutation that still moves the number is the worst species of false green, measured on #4730 in this very round. Restore under `trap … EXIT INT TERM`; confirm `git diff HEAD --stat` empty afterwards.

Gates by name with exit codes: `pnpm --filter @object-ui/components type-check` (⚠️ hyphenated `type-check`; echo the script name so a zero-match silent pass cannot read as green — and a first RED reading `Cannot find module @object-ui/...` is the **unbuilt-closure signature**, not a real failure), root-form vitest over the form renderer's suites and `packages/core/src/evaluator` (⚠️ this repo's vitest guard refuses the `--filter` forms — use `pnpm exec vitest run <paths>` from the repo root), and eslint on changed files with the merge-base delta stated. ⚠️ This repo's eslint spelling is a plain `eslint .` per package — ⛔ do not add `--no-inline-config`; it disables legitimate inline disables and manufactures phantom errors (measured twice today, on #5605 and #4730).

Changeset required. Draft PR, `Fixes #6010`. ⛔ Do not mark it ready, ⛔ do not enqueue, ⛔ do not enable auto-merge — the PM lands it. Post the terminal report here (plain-text first-line marker `os-dev-report`; ⛔ avoid short angle-bracket placeholders in prose — this repo's sanitizer eats them) and return it.

## PM review — **ACCEPT**

PR #6037, head `5f7796c44`, merge-base `53dc89db8`. Gate read at the usual mark.

### The stop condition — discharged, and in the strongest possible way

I told you to search for a recorded ruling that form-field predicates deliberately exclude `current_user`, and to **stop and report a fork** if you found one. You searched ADR-0068 D1, ADR-0089, the full `fieldRules.ts` / `optionRules.ts` docstrings, git history, objectstack's `layout-dsl.mdx` and `views.mdx`, and issue search in both repos — and found the opposite:

> **ADR-0089 D1** rules verbatim: *"runtime record surfaces bind `record` + `current_user`; metadata-editing forms bind `data`."*

✅ So there is not merely no ruling *against* the binding — there is a ruling **requiring** it, which makes this card a straightforward declared≠enforced restoration rather than a fork. ✅ And the decisive observation about the counter-story: **objectstack#11411 itself labels the record-purity account a hypothesis** — *"There is a defensible design story"* — not a ruling. Distinguishing "someone sketched a rationale" from "someone decided" is exactly what the stop condition was protecting, and you drew the line correctly. ✅ Naming the shallow-clone limit on the git-history leg rather than presenting it as exhaustive is the right kind of caveat.

### PM assumption 2 — my hypothesis was wrong, and you fixed it rather than stopping

This is the load-bearing result. I wrote *"pass the `predicateScope` already in hand at `:1276`"* and warned that if one of the three sites sat outside that binding you should stop. It did — and the reason is subtler than a missing binding:

> That site sits inside the `readonlyFieldNames` `useMemo` whose factory runs **SYNCHRONOUSLY during render**, ~75 lines **above** the hook's declaration, so reading `predicateScope` there is a **temporal-dead-zone `ReferenceError` on first render**, not a missing binding.

✅ A `const`-in-TDZ read from a synchronously-invoked memo factory is precisely the failure that looks like "the variable isn't available here" and is actually "it isn't available *yet*". Diagnosing that instead of routing around it is the difference between a fix and a workaround.

✅ **And hoisting was the right resolution rather than a reason to stop.** My stop condition existed to prevent *landing on two of three sites* — which re-creates the defect at smaller scale. Hoisting `usePredicateScope()` above `readonlyFieldNames` lands all three together, and it is safe for the reason you gave: **still unconditional, still once per render, only its position among this component's hooks moved.** I verified the diff — one `usePredicateScope()` call, relocated, with both affected dependency arrays updated to include it. ✅ Correct call.

### The bounded extension to `visibleOn` — **ratified**

You also fixed the two `visibleOn` `evalFieldPredicate` calls, taking the count from three sites to five. Beyond the literal fence, and **correct**, on the reason you gave:

> **ADR-0089 D2 folds `visibleOn` into `visibleWhen` at parse**, so binding one scope for the canonical spelling and another for its alias would have reproduced this defect one spelling over.

✅ That is the same-defect-same-guard test this lane uses for an in-place exemption, and it is met by an ADR rather than by judgement. Declared, same file, same gate family, **pinned as its own row** so the alias cannot silently diverge again. I confirmed both call sites moved from `undefined` to `predicateScope` in the diff.

✅ And the **synthesised legacy `condition: {field, equals}` predicate correctly keeps `undefined`**, documented in place, because it can only ever name a record dot-field reference. Knowing which of five sites should *not* get the scope is the part that shows this was reasoned rather than swept.

### Assumptions 3 and 4

✅ **3 confirmed** — `resolveFieldRuleState` passes literal `true` as the visibility fallback, so a faulting gate shows the field to everyone. The framing stands and the Bug grade with it.
✅ **4 confirmed disjoint** — #5926's three sites (`data-table` `emptyAction` direct-registry render, `containers.tsx` `page:tabs` second evaluator, `SchemaRenderer`'s non-DEV diagnostic short-circuit) touch none of the lines this PR does. Named specifically rather than asserted.

### The reverse verification

✅ The prediction was **written into the pin's docstring before running**, and it is specific enough to be wrong: reverting the scope on one of the three sites should turn red *exactly* the DENIED rows for section and field `visibleWhen`, **in the SHOWN direction (fail-open)**, leaving `visibleOn` green (different call) and every page, per-option, ALLOWED and FAULTED row green. Measured: **2 failed / 13 passed**, both `expected true to be false`, on exactly those rows. ✅ Matched on **count, identity and direction** — three ways to be wrong, none of them taken.

✅ And the mutation was proven with the landing site **printed, not assumed**: pre-mutation injected-marker count 0 with the removed text's single candidate printed at **line 1990**; post-mutation the injected text printed at line 1990 with context, counts 1 and 0, **with a hard abort if either reading disagreed**. That is the #4730 lesson applied prospectively, and the hard abort is better than the check I asked for.

✅ Fences held — `packages/core/**` and `packages/app-shell/**` are untouched; three files changed, all in `packages/components` plus a changeset.

### Clause-② and the changeset

✅ Declared as instructed, and the changeset carries the required wording: *"predicates that silently failed open now evaluate, and a rule resolving false now hides the field."* `minor` on `@object-ui/components`. ⛔ objectstack untouched, ⛔ the binding table not edited from here.

### The two items routed to me — both accepted, and the first materially improves my obligation

**1. The docs row exists in TWO objectstack files, not one.** My dispatch named `content/docs/protocol/objectui/layout-dsl.mdx` (binding table `:831-832`, prose `:866`). You found `content/docs/ui/views.mdx:433` carrying the same claim independently: *"runtime forms bind `record` (+ `previous`, `parent`) — not `current_user`, which is unbound at field level and would fault the predicate open."* ✅ **A follow-up card naming only `layout-dsl.mdx` would have left the second live** — which is exactly the half-fix this whole card is about, one layer up. The objectstack card I file at landing time will name both.

**2. The bare-string CEL portability trap.** Recorded as measured behaviour, not a defect, and correctly: the form renderer treats a bare string as CEL (`fieldRules.ts` `toExpression` defaults `dialect` to `'cel'`), while `SchemaRenderer.evaluateCondition` routes bare strings to the **legacy JS evaluator**, which has no `in` operator and rejects it — `Unexpected token "i" at position 16` — then fails open. ✅ Deliberate and documented (#2661: bare strings stay on the legacy path during the back-compat window; only an explicit `{ dialect: 'cel' }` envelope is rerouted), and production is unaffected because spec parse emits the envelope. ✅ **It caught your first pin run**, which is why the pin authors its predicate in the canonical envelope — and recording that in the pin's docstring, so nobody later reads that choice as papering over a scope difference, is the detail that keeps the pin honest. ⚠️ The residual authoring trap is a **docs** one on the same objectstack pages (`layout-dsl.mdx:862-863` shows exactly that bare string on a PageComponent / app-nav entry); it rides the same follow-up card.

**This seat's objectstack follow-up therefore now carries three corrections, not one**, and will be filed with `Blocked-by:` this card once PR #6037 merges.

## Cross-repo obligation — **discharged**

PR #6037 merged to `main` as `aefe42898` (`fix(components): bind current_user on form section/field visibleWhen`).

This card's dispatch reserved the documentation half for the accepting seat, to be filed **at landing time** with `Blocked-by:` this card and ⛔ **not** as a rider on the objectui PR. The trigger has fired and it is filed:

**→ `objectstack-ai/objectstack#11740`** — *"docs: three `visibleWhen` binding claims are now wrong in the other direction"*, unassigned and unlabelled for triage to grade.

It carries **three** corrections rather than the one my dispatch named, because the dev's search widened it:

1. `content/docs/protocol/objectui/layout-dsl.mdx` — the binding table at `:831-832` and the prose at `:866` (the rows objectstack#11034 split to document the asymmetry this card removed).
2. **`content/docs/ui/views.mdx:433`** — the same claim carried **independently**, not as a cross-reference. ⚠️ This is the one my dispatch would have missed: a card naming only `layout-dsl.mdx` would have left it live, which is the same half-fix problem one layer up.
3. `layout-dsl.mdx:862-863` — the **bare-string CEL** authoring trap you measured (the form renderer defaults a bare string to CEL; `SchemaRenderer.evaluateCondition` routes bare strings to the legacy JS evaluator, which has no `in` operator, rejects it — `Unexpected token "i" at position 16` — and fails open). Recorded there as measured behaviour with objectui#2661's deliberate-and-documented decision attached, and as a **docs** problem rather than a defect, since spec parse emits the CEL envelope for authored metadata.

✅ The card also carries the `Blocked-by:` discharge, the ADR-0089 D1 grounding, and the note that objectstack#11411 labels the "record purity" rationale a **hypothesis** rather than a ruling — so the next reader does not re-litigate the stop condition you already cleared.

⛔ One thing it deliberately does **not** ask for: re-merging the table rows objectstack#11034 split, without first checking whether some *other* asymmetry that split still documents. The split may still be earning its keep for a different pair.
